claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3510 - CIA unvouchered funds (CIA Act of 1949, sec. 8)
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3510(b): 'The sums made available to the Agency may be expended without regard to the provisions of law and regulations relating to the expenditure of Government funds; and for objects of a confidential, extraordinary, or emergency nature, such expenditures to be accounted for solely on the certificate of the Director and every such certificate shall be deemed a sufficient voucher for the amount therein certified.'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3510 - CIA unvouchered funds (CIA Act of 1949, sec. 8)
claims.text: The provision originates as section 8 of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949, enacted 20 June 1949.
50 U.S.C. 3510 permits certain expenditures to be accounted for solely on the certificate of the agency head.
50 U.S.C. 3510 permits certain intelligence expenditures to be accounted for solely on the certificate of the agency head, with that certificate deemed a sufficient voucher.

edges.label: Unvouchered CIA spending sits inside the NIP and outside all expenditure law
edges.note: 50 U.S.C. 3510(b) permits Agency sums to be expended without regard to laws and regulations governing expenditure of government funds, accounted for solely on the Director's certificate. The CIA is funded within the National Intelligence Program. Attested by the statute.

edges.label: An activity funded from unvouchered CIA money never touches the appropriations SAP tripwire
edges.note: Section 8009 binds only funds appropriated by the annual Defense Appropriations Act; unvouchered Agency spending under 50 U.S.C. 3510 is neither DoD appropriated funds nor subject to normal expenditure law. Reasoned inference from the two texts; no document asserts this has occurred.
